Subject: Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) — post-demo recap & next steps

Hi John / SRE team,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — really appreciate the time. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can get a targeted PoC going: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Redwood Private: control plane that can be customer-managed in your VPC or run as a private control plane (no public ingress).
- Air-gapped/on-prem option: full inference runtime can be deployed without egress; we ship an on-prem package for regulated environments.
- Differentiators vs hyperscalers: consistent API across hosted/dedicated/private, high-throughput runtime with batching/KV cache, and tooling to benchmark cost/latency.

Proposed next tests (to validate fit):
1) Network connectivity test — verify required ports and firewall rules between your VPC and (optionally) our control plane.
2) Air-gap feasibility run — deploy the runtime in an isolated staging network with a sample model (we can provide quantized artifacts).
3) Perf/quality test — 1-GPU perf run at ~8k sequence to validate latency/throughput and compare to your current hyperscaler endpoints.

What we need from you to start:
- A network diagram (VPC subnets/egress points) and a point-of-contact on SRE who can run the connectivity test.
- If you're considering fully air-gapped, indicate whether you want a customer-managed control plane (in-VPC) or a fully offline on-prem package.
- Any procurement or security checklist items we should pre-fill (SOC2, data handling, etc.).

Attached: redwood_private_vpc_summary.pdf (high-level architecture + checklist).

If that looks good, I’ll loop in Marissa (solutions engineering) and Aditya (platform) to coordinate the test plan and provide the network checklist. Available slots for the connectivity test next week: Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

Thanks,

John — great questions. Looping in Marissa (solutions) and Aditya (platform) to scope the technical plan. Answers & concrete plan below: 

Control plane connectivity
- Option A (recommended for most customers): Customer-managed control plane inside your VPC. No public internet required for control plane → we provide IaC templates and a small operator image. That means inbound/outbound firewall rules are only internal to your network.
- Option B: Redwood-managed private control plane that is reachable over outbound TLS from your VPC to a dedicated control plane endpoint (mutual TLS available). This requires a small set of outbound ports (443) and mutual auth; we supply exact CIDR/IPs and cert fingerprints during onboarding.

Air-gapped/on-prem feasibility
- Full air-gap supported: on-prem package includes runtime, model artifacts, and an offline installer. No telemetry is sent by default; you opt-in to any usage metrics. Key management: supports customer KMS/HSM and local key storage (no escrow required).

How we compare to hyperscalers (brief):
- Hyperscalers: easy managed endpoints but control plane lives with vendor, limited control over private networking, and often higher per-token cost for this class of low-latency workloads.
- Redwood: consistent API regardless of deployment, ability to run the control plane in-VPC or fully offline, and runtime optimizations (KV caching, continuous batching, quantization profiles) that improve throughput/cost for production inference.

Proposed immediate next steps (we can run these as a coordinated checklist):
1) SRE: run network connectivity test (we'll provide checklist). Target: allow either in-VPC operator deployment or allow outbound TLS to our private control plane IPs.
2) Platform test: we'll provide a small model artifact (quantized) and an air-gapped installer to deploy to your staging host. Run perf test: 1x A10G (or equivalent) with 8k seq, 100 concurrent sessions (or scaled-down if hardware limited).
3) Security/procurement: we'll share SOC2 report and a short data retention write-up. Marissa will start the security package.

Attachments: network_test_checklist.xlsx (checklist for SRE + ports/runbook).

Marissa / Aditya — can you confirm:
- Marissa: SOC2/attestation and security packet — can you drop the docs link?
- Aditya: can the platform team prepare a sample quantized model + short perf script? Target deliverable by EOD Friday.

John — can you confirm which option you prefer (customer-managed control plane in-VPC vs Redwood-managed outbound TLS)? Also which day next week works for the connectivity run (Tue/Wed afternoon PT suggested).

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
